code-architecture.entrypoints: The crate builds a `cargo-enforcer` binary (see Cargo.toml `[[bin]]`). `src/main.rs` is the thin CLI shell: it reads the subcommand argument (skipping the leading `enforcer` arg that cargo injects for `cargo enforcer <check>`), parses it into a `Command`, and calls `command.run()`.
code-architecture.commands-dispatch: `src/t/command.rs` defines the `Command` enum. `Command::run` dispatches to each check's module (e.g. `file_sizes::run()`). Adding a check = new enum variant + new check module.
code-architecture.shared-code: `src/s/` holds static data. `src/c/` is shared logic. `src/t/` is shared types.
code-architecture.check-impls: Aside from the shared-code, each check is implemented in its own folder under `src/checks` (Checks related to tree structure are grouped in `src/checks/tree_structure/`). In each folder, there is a description of the check in desc.xml.
code-architecture.check-anatomy: The conventional layout of a check folder (see `mod_location`, `mod_over_file` for minimal examples): - `mod.rs` — declares the submodules and does `pub use main::run;`. - `main.rs` — `pub fn run() -> bool` is the entrypoint. It typically calls `scan::src_files(_check_file)` and hands the result to `report::print`. `run` returns `true` when the check FAILED (any violations), matching `Command::run`. - `report.rs` — `print(passed, violations) -> bool`, wrapping `c::report::summary`. - Optional `t.rs` (or `t/`) for check-local types; extra files/subfolders for bigger checks (e.g. `import_rules/check/`, `call_rules/find/`). Wiring a new check requires three edits beyond the folder: add `pub mod <name>;` to `src/checks/mod.rs`, a `Command` variant in `src/t/command.rs`, and a match arm in `src/run.rs`. Private fns are prefixed with `_` per the project convention.
code-architecture.check-docs: Every check folder carries: - `desc.xml` — the human spec of the check: a `<desc>` summary plus the `<rules>` (and any `<exemption>`) it enforces. READ THIS FIRST when implementing or changing a check — it is the source of truth for behavior.
code-architecture.shared-helpers: Reusable building blocks the checks lean on, so you rarely need bespoke fs/AST code: - `c::scan::src_files(check)` — iterates every `.rs` under the existing src dirs (`s::EXISTING_SRC_DIRS`, i.e. `src` and `tests`), calling `check(&Path) -> Outcome<V>` per file and tallying results into `(passed: usize, Vec<V>)`. - `t::Outcome<V>` — `Skipped | Passed | Failed(V)`; the return type of a per-file check. `t::ItemsViolation { path: String, items: Vec<String> }` is the common violation payload (used by type/static/trait-location, etc.). - `c::files` — `rs(dir_name) -> Vec<PathBuf>` (glob), `parse(path) -> syn::File`. - `c::path` — `rel(path)` (root-relative display string), `under_dir(path, name)` (any path component equals `name`), `common_file_kind(path)` (`Some("c"|"cnst"|"s"|"t" |"ext_traits")` when the file stem is a common name), `parent_name`, `is_mod_or_lib`. Common dirs/files are the five names `c, cnst, s, t, ext_traits`. - `c::ast` — `is_public(vis)`, plus `use`-tree helpers (`glob_module`, `exposed_names`). AST work uses the `syn` crate (`syn::Item::*`, etc.). - `c::report::summary(name, passed, success_msg, violations, on_fail)` — prints the cyan header, the green success line or the pass/fail counts, and invokes `on_fail` to render details. Use `colored::Colorize` for coloring (`.bold()`, `.red()`…).
code-architecture.enforcer.toml: `src/s/file_config.rs` exposes the `FILE_CONFIG` static: a `LazyLock` that reads `enforcer.toml` from the project root (`ROOT`), allows users to configure the checks.
code-architecture.std-out: All checks should print good messages to the console about the results using nice color schemes following the pattern already laid out. A message of the "all passed" sort if all pass, and if failures should print details, so the user knows where the failures happened and can click links, if possible, to go fix. The number of passes and failures should be printed in all cases, like it is for the existing checks.
